column4: Close-up of a single coal-black hooded congregant in a pew, bent over an open ledger, the deep hood hiding the face completely in black shadow. On the ledger page are rows of small orange tally marks and checkboxes. Behind, a dark stone wall with a long hanging scroll covered in the same rows of tally marks. No text lettering.

Same young woman as the portrait, bust shot, facing the viewer, eyes open and steady, holding the closed black shears upright. Her old porcelain doll shell is bursting off her: white porcelain chips, a white maid headband piece and a copper winding key fly outward away from her body, and short cut tan-gold thread ends spring up. Underneath she is a living human: natural skin, white blouse with black ribbon bow and orange brooch, no ball joints, no seams. Flat ivory background. No text.

Same composition as the first reference, but this is a living human hand and wrist: natural skin with soft knuckles, no ball joints, no wrist ring, the white blouse cuff of the portrait at the left edge. The hand is clenched in a tight fist. Flat ivory background. No text.

Same camera and book shaft as the reference, but instead of a porcelain boot, a bare living human foot (natural skin, five toes, no joints) hangs just above the coal-dark soil, toes pointing down, a clear gap between toe and soil. The hem of a layered black, ivory and orange skirt at the top edge. No strings, no text.
